shipped.warum: In 1886 Williston's shipping point was Archer, eleven miles off. By 1895 the town was on two railroads, which in 1898 charged the same ten cents a crate; it was incorporated in 1897, and in 1905 the legislature declared the incorporation lawful after the fact.
shipped.quelle: Florida State Gazetteer 1886; Engineering News 1891; Manufacturers' Record 1893; Florida Railroad Gazetteer 1895; Railroad Commission of Florida 1898; Laws of Florida 1905; Polk's Gazetteer 1907–1908.

shipped.warum: Phosphate dug by hand in pits around Albion and Morriston, much of it in the 1890s by leased state prisoners, most of them Black, of whom the lessee counted forty dead in two years. Nearly all of it went to Europe, until the war stopped the ships in 1914.
shipped.quelle: Manufacturers' Record 1893; Reports of the Commissioner of Agriculture of Florida 1893–1902; USGS Bulletin 604 (1915); Florida Geological Survey annual reports 1915–1922.

shipped.warum: Cucumbers from 20,000 crates in 1897 to over 200,000 in 1919, nine to twenty-two cars a day, consigned to commission men in the North. In 1923 they brought nearly three quarters of the farms' income; the work was done by day labourers, contract pickers and sharecroppers whom no source names.
shipped.quelle: Ocala Evening Star 1897–1916; USDA Soil Survey 1904; Florida's Financial and Industrial Record 1910; SAL Shippers Guide 1914; Cammack 1916; USDA Bulletin 462 (1917); Lakeland Evening Telegram 1919; Florida Experiment Station Bulletin 175 (1925).
shipped.zk: First cars · Trainload · 1919 · Who did the work

planned.warum: Jesse M. Willis, the people he enslaved, and a settlement between Marion and Levy counties; Yulee's Florida Railroad to Cedar Key passes it by. In 1886 Archer, eleven miles off, is its shipping point.
planned.quelle: Florida State Gazetteer 1886; Ocala Banner 1911; Makers of America 1911.

planned.warum: Convict leasing, the lynching of Wash Bradley at Bronson in 1904, and Rosewood in January 1923, from the sources of their time; the missing voices named.
planned.quelle: NAACP, Thirty Years of Lynching (1919); Florida newspapers 1902–1923; state reports on convicts.

planned.warum: Montbrook Army Air Field, 1942–1944: how a war came to a farm town and left again.
planned.quelle: Army Air Forces records and newspapers (to be found).

missing.warum: Its own economic and historical space, older than Williston: port, fishery, cedar for pencils. Not a subject at this stage; it appears only where the rails, timber and work of Williston, Bronson and Rosewood lead there. A later stage “Cedar Key and the coast” remains open.
missing.quelle: Seaboard Air Line Shippers Guide 1914 and others.

missing.warum: “A Documented History of the Incident Which Occurred at Rosewood, Florida, in January 1923”, submitted to the Florida Board of Regents on 22 December 1993. It is the guide to the sources of January 1923 but not certainly in the public domain; it is summarized and cited, not printed.
missing.quelle: M. D. Jones, L. E. Rivers, D. R. Colburn, R. T. Dye, W. R. Rogers (1993).

missing.warum: A figure found only in recent accounts of Williston's cucumber trade, for example as something “reportedly” shipped in the 1920s (Levy County Journal, 26 October 2006). No source of the time carrying it has been found. The period figures are nine cars in a day (1907), twenty-two cars a day at the height of the season (1910) and thirteen to twenty cars daily (1919); a local history of 1983 gives seventeen. Recent texts are under copyright and are cited, not printed.
missing.quelle: Levy County Journal, 26 Oct. 2006; Search for Yesterday, ch. 13 (Levy County Archives Committee, 1983), both in the University of Florida Digital Collections.

missing.kurz: Sanborn maps of Williston (1930) and Bronson (1924)
missing.warum: In the public domain but not yet digitized by the Library of Congress; the map layer starts with the Williston sheets of January 1923.
missing.quelle: Library of Congress, Sanborn Maps Collection.

missing.warum: The Experiment Station followed Bulletin 175 with “Factors Affecting Cucumber Yields, Costs, and Profits: A Study of the Williston Area, Florida, for 1923, 1928, 1930 and 1932”. Published after 1930, its copyright status has to be checked before anything is printed from it.
missing.quelle: University of Florida Agricultural Experiment Station, 1930s.
